terminal.description: A shell in your workspace, already pointed at the offline lab model.

tasks.title: Build the messages for one question
tasks.description:
In `src/ask.ts`, implement `buildMessages(question: string): Message[]`.

Return exactly two messages, in this order:

1. `{ role: 'system', content: SYSTEM_PROMPT }`
2. `{ role: 'user', content: question }` with the question unchanged

The check calls `buildMessages` with a customer question and compares the array it returns.
nextSteps: Read the lesson section on messages and roles.
Return an array literal with the two message objects.
Run `node src/demo.ts` and look at what buildMessages prints.
hints: A message is a plain object with a `role` and a `content`.
The order matters: instructions for the model first, then what the customer asked.
Use the `SYSTEM_PROMPT` constant for the first message and the `question` argument for the second.

tasks.title: Send the question and read the reply
tasks.description:
Implement `ask(question: string, client?: OpenAI): Promise<string>`.

- Send one chat completion request through `client` with `model: MODEL` and `messages: buildMessages(question)`.
- Return the text of the first choice's message. If the content is `null`, return an empty string.

The check asks two questions through the lab model and compares the text. It also calls `ask` with a fake client to make sure your request goes through the client you are given and names `MODEL`. The lab model starts its answer with "Moss here." only when it sees the system message.
nextSteps: Call `client.chat.completions.create` with the model and the messages.
Await the response and print it once to see its shape.
Return the content of the first choice's message.
Run `node src/demo.ts` and read the answer.
hints: Keep using the `client` parameter. Do not create a second client inside the function.
The response has a `choices` array. Each choice has a `message`.
The text is at `res.choices[0].message.content`, which TypeScript says can be null, so fall back to ''.

tasks.title: Read the finish reason and usage
tasks.description:
Implement `askWithDetails(question: string, maxTokens: number, client?: OpenAI): Promise<ReplyDetails>`.

Send the same request as `ask`, with `max_tokens` set to `maxTokens`. Return:

- `text`: the reply content (or `''`)
- `finishReason`: the `finish_reason` of the first choice
- `promptTokens`, `completionTokens`, `totalTokens`: copied from the response's `usage`

The check calls it once with 200 tokens, where the reply fits and ends with `stop`, and once with 6 tokens, where the model is cut off and ends with `length`.
nextSteps: Copy the request from `ask` and add `max_tokens`.
Keep the first choice in a variable so you can read two fields from it.
Run `node src/demo.ts` and compare the 200 token and 8 token results.
hints: Everything you need is in one response object: the choice and the usage sit side by side.
`usage` uses snake_case names like `prompt_tokens`, while `ReplyDetails` uses camelCase.
TypeScript marks `usage` as optional, so read it with `res.usage?.` and a fallback of 0.
